transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Carla Colman.
The Associated Press estimates that two Senate seats and nearly 50 House races have not yet
been called.
Erin Covey is with The Cook Political Report.
She says it is possible for Democrats to claim several more House seats.
She's been watching undecided House races in North Carolina.
I think this was one state where Republicans' turnout problems were particularly acute.
They had a very, initially a competitive statewide race at the top of the ticket, but it became
increasingly clear that former Governor Roy Cooper was going to win that Senate race by
a resounding margin, and Republicans pulled out.
And now at this point, it looks like Republicans may only hold four out of 14 seats in that
state.
She spoke to NPR's Morning Edition.
Two uncalled Senate races are in Alaska and Mississippi.
In Alaska, Democratic challenger Mary Peltola has a slight edge over Republican incumbent
Dan Sullivan.
In Mississippi, Democratic challenger Scott Colom has only a few dozen votes ahead of
Republican incumbent Cindy Hyde Smith.
Elon Musk may face congressional investigations following Democrats' victory in the midterm
elections, and Pierre's Katie McHugh has more.
Musk spent more than $400 million backing Republican candidates, including at least
half of that to support Ken Paxton in the Texas Senate race.
Paxton lost to Democrat James Talarico.
Many Democrats say they plan to investigate Musk and his businesses.
In particular, they want to focus on his time running the Department of Government Efficiency.
The founder of SpaceX and Tesla has gotten billions of dollars worth of government contracts
since Donald Trump returned to office.
Katie McHugh, NPR News, New York.
Israel is taking the next step toward forming a government.
Israel's president has started meeting with political parties, and, as Daniel Esther reports,
he's seeking to appoint one leader to try to form a governing coalition.
Israel's president began by meeting a far-right Jewish party.
The party's leaders said Arab-led parties did not have the legitimacy to be in a governing
coalition.
The president warned the party against racism.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu says last week's election in Israel was "stolen,"
alleging Arab voter fraud.
Israel's top elections officials said casting doubt on the vote poses a danger to democracy.
The majority of those voted into Israel's parliament, the Knesset, are right-wing.
Israeli analyst Dalia Shenlin.
The Knesset will be dominated by ideologically right-wing parties.
And that will also set the terms of the agenda, possibly gather that kind of majority support
for various military policies coming up.
Israel and the U.S. have considered new strikes on Iran.
Daniel Estrin, NPR News, Tel Aviv.
You're listening to NPR.
Weather forecasters say there's been flash flooding this morning in parts of southeastern
Tennessee and northern Georgia.
The National Weather Service says this flooding is catastrophic and widespread.
Things have gone up for Polk County, Tennessee, and in Georgia's Fannin County, there are
evacuations underway.
A court in Hong Kong has handed prominent democracy activist Joshua Wong a 10-year sentence.
This is under a national security law imposed by China.
And NPR's Jennifer Pack reports Wong's supporters say the charge is fabricated.
Wong is already serving a prison sentence for subversion.
He was due to be released in two months until he received this latest sentence.
Wong is convicted of foreign collusion by rallying other countries to impose sanctions
or blockades on Hong Kong and China in 2020.
Fellow Hong Kong activists and friend Chongqing Kuang is relieved the sentence isn't longer.
Wong is the face of youth activism in Hong Kong.
The U.S. Congressional Executive Commission on China says Hong Kong's courts are being
weaponized for repression, remarks like these according to China's foreign ministry are
irresponsible.
Jennifer Pack, NPR News, Beijing.
There have been several bomb threats made against flights in Europe today.
Multiple flights have been diverted.
Authorities in Bulgaria, Czechia, and Italy say planes have landed without incident.
These threats come after several similar threats were issued earlier this week against passenger
planes in Europe.
No device has been found.
No one has been harmed.
This is NPR.

topics.text: Democrats may gain more House seats as dozens of races remain uncalled, including in North Carolina
Two Senate races remain uncalled: Alaska's Peltola-Sullivan and Mississippi's Colom-Hyde Smith
Elon Musk faces possible congressional investigations after spending over $400 million backing Republicans
Israeli President begins consultations with parties to appoint a leader to form a governing coalition
Netanyahu alleges Arab voter fraud in last week's Israeli election, drawing warnings from election officials
Flash flooding catastrophic in southeastern Tennessee and northern Georgia; evacuations underway in Fannin County
Hong Kong court sentences democracy activist Joshua Wong to 10 years under China's national security law
Bomb threats against passenger flights in Bulgaria, Czechia, and Italy lead to diversions; no devices found
